journal.text: Initiated a diversified defensive/relative-strength portfolio with $42,000 invested and $8,000 cash reserved. The broad technology complex is in a pronounced downswing, while ORLY, PAYX, AEP, EXC, CCEP, and VRSK are near recent highs and showed resilience into the March 31 close. ORLY supplies the strongest long-term trend; PAYX and VRSK add lower-volatility business services; AEP and EXC capture utility leadership; CCEP adds consumer defensiveness. Dollar sizing limits overnight-gap execution risk. Reconsider any holding after a decisive break of its March support/roughly 20-day trend, persistent relative weakness, or if growth/technology leadership clearly reasserts itself; avoid adding merely because of a decline. Retain cash for better confirmation or new leadership.

Held the six-position defensive portfolio and retained $8,000 cash. Through April 1, ORLY, PAYX, EXC, CCEP, and VRSK remained near recent highs, while AEP's modest pullback stayed above its late-March breakout area. Growth and semiconductor names remain broadly damaged despite scattered rebounds, so there is not yet enough evidence to rotate or spend the reserve. Reconsider on decisive support breaks (approximately ORLY 1390, PAYX 150, AEP 102, EXC 44, CCEP 84, VRSK 292), persistent relative weakness, or a sustained leadership shift toward growth; deploy cash only after stronger confirmation.

Added a $7,000 MNST position while retaining roughly $1,000 cash. MNST closed at 59.36 on April 2, a 30-session high, after a steady sequence of higher highs and higher lows from mid-March; this provides a fresh defensive consumer leader without rotating out of the six resilient incumbents. ORLY remains above its roughly 1390 support, PAYX/EXC/CCEP/VRSK remain near recent highs, and AEP's two-day easing still holds above the late-March breakout zone. Broad growth and semiconductors are rebounding but remain well below February levels, so no wholesale risk-on rotation is justified. Reconsider MNST on a decisive close below roughly 57, and retain the prior support checks for existing holdings; rotate only if relative strength deteriorates or growth leadership becomes sustained.

Held the seven-position defensive portfolio with about $1,000 cash. The April 3 broad selloff was severe across technology, semiconductors, cyclicals, and consumer discretionary names, but the portfolio showed exceptional relative strength: ORLY, AEP, EXC, CCEP, VRSK, and MNST all closed higher, while PAYX slipped less than 1% and remained above 150. This confirms rather than weakens the defensive thesis, and no alternative justifies taking overnight gap risk after a one-day shock. Reconsider after decisive closes below approximately ORLY 1390, PAYX 150, AEP 107, EXC 45.5-46, CCEP 86-87, VRSK 298, or MNST 57-58; otherwise retain leaders and cash until the market stabilizes or sustained new leadership emerges.

Reduced risk by exiting PAYX and VRSK, the two weakest medium-term holdings, and moved their proceeds to cash rather than buying into an accelerating market-wide breakdown. PAYX closed at 143.32, decisively below the prior 150 support and below its January 24 close; VRSK closed at 284.99, below the 292-298 support area and near its late-January level. Both fell about 6.6% on April 4 and closed near their session lows on elevated volume. Retained ORLY, AEP, EXC, CCEP, and MNST because their 50-session trends and relative strength remain materially better, although Friday tested or breached near-term support. Reconsider further reductions if ORLY closes clearly below 1389, AEP below 102-104, EXC below 44-45, CCEP below 83-84, or MNST below 57; redeploy cash only after stabilization, constructive higher lows, or sustained leadership emerges.

Further reduced exposure after three retained defensive names decisively lost their stated support levels on April 7. ORLY closed 1333.84, well below 1389 and near the session low; AEP closed 101.57 after falling through 102-104; CCEP closed 82.99 after a second weak session below 83-84. Their breakdowns occurred despite broad intraday rebounds and therefore no longer justify full positions. Retained EXC because 44.69 is only marginally inside its 44-45 review zone and above the 43.95 intraday low, and retained MNST because it stabilized at 57.11 after testing 56. Cash rises to roughly 70% rather than chasing highly volatile one-day rebounds across growth. Reconsider EXC on a decisive close below 44 and MNST below 56-57; redeploy only after a durable higher low, follow-through rally, or clear relative-strength leadership.

Exited MNST after its stabilization failed: it fell from 57.11 to 55.01 on April 8, closed near the 54.84 session low, decisively breached the stated 56-57 review zone, and did so on 19.3 million shares, nearly twice April 4 volume. Retained EXC because its 44.49 close remained above the decisive-breach threshold of 44, its 44.02 low held that area, and it continues to show materially better relative strength than the broadly declining universe. With April 8 producing another market-wide intraday reversal and most candidates still below broken support, kept the sale proceeds in cash rather than buying an unconfirmed rebound. Reconsider EXC on a decisive close below 44; redeploy cash only after follow-through strength, a durable higher low, or clear relative-strength leadership.

Partially redeployed cash after April 9 produced a broad, high-volume upside reversal, but kept roughly half the account in cash because one session does not yet establish a durable uptrend. Bought CPRT, COST, and ROST because they showed the clearest relative-strength leadership: CPRT closed at 58.52 near its 58.97 high and above every prior close in the 20-session window; COST closed at 965.19 near its 967.46 high and essentially recovered its pre-breakdown level; ROST closed at 137 near its 139.29 high and above its prior 132.37 closing high. Retained EXC because its 44.30 close still held the stated decisive-close threshold of 44 despite an intraday breach, while providing defensive diversification. Reconsider new positions if the reversal fails and CPRT closes below roughly 54-55, COST below 900-916, or ROST below 126-130; exit EXC on a decisive close below 44. Add exposure only on follow-through or constructive higher lows.

Added one measured WMT position while retaining substantial cash because April 10 was a broad retracement rather than convincing market follow-through. WMT was a notable exception: it rose from 89.60 to 90.61, closed above every prior close in the 20-session window, and finished in the upper part of its 88.16-91.87 range after April 9's high-volume advance. Existing leaders also validated retention: CPRT edged to another 20-session closing high at 58.66, ROST advanced to 138.89, COST held essentially flat at 964.31 despite reaching 993.41, and EXC strengthened to 45.12 above the 44 risk threshold. Keep roughly 43% cash while broad conditions remain unstable. Reconsider WMT on a decisive close below roughly 85-88, CPRT below 54-55, COST below 900-916, ROST below 126-130, and EXC below 44; add further exposure only if leadership persists or the broader market develops durable follow-through.

Added one measured FAST position while retaining roughly one-third of the account in cash. April 11 broadened the rebound, but many former leaders remain below their pre-shock ranges, so full deployment is still premature. FAST provided unusually clear fresh leadership: it rose from 75.79 to 80.64 on 7.56 million shares, closed near its 81.31 high, and decisively exceeded every prior close in the 20-session window. Existing holdings also continued to validate retention: CPRT, ROST, and WMT each made new 20-session closing highs; EXC recovered to 46; and COST held near 963 after its sharp rebound. Reconsider FAST on a decisive close below roughly 74-76, WMT below 85-88, CPRT below 54-55, COST below 900-916, ROST below 126-130, and EXC below 44. Add more exposure only if leadership and broader follow-through persist.

Added a measured TRI position while preserving about 23% cash. April 14 was mixed rather than broad confirmation, but TRI supplied fresh low-volatility leadership: it advanced from 172.68 to 176.36, closed near its 176.56 high, and exceeded every prior close in the 20-session window after three consecutive gains. Existing positions remain technically constructive: FAST, WMT, ROST, and CPRT held near fresh highs; COST advanced to 979.32; and EXC reached 46.86. The portfolio therefore stays focused on demonstrated relative strength rather than the still-damaged high-beta groups. Reconsider TRI on a decisive close below roughly 167-170. Retain prior risk levels of FAST 74-76, WMT 85-88, CPRT 54-55, COST 900-916, ROST 126-130, and EXC 44; deploy remaining cash only if leadership broadens and follow-through persists.

Added a measured CRWD position while retaining roughly 14% cash. April 15 still lacked broad confirmation, but CRWD provided a credible fresh leadership signal: it rose from 378.66 to 392.80, closed above every earlier close in the 20-session window, traded as high as 400.02, and volume expanded to 5.20 million shares. Existing positions remain constructive overall: TRI surged to 181.70 on unusually strong volume, while FAST and CPRT posted fresh closing highs; modest pullbacks in COST, ROST, WMT, and EXC did not threaten established risk levels. Reconsider CRWD on a decisive close below roughly 360-368. Retain risk levels of TRI 167-170, FAST 74-76, WMT 85-88, CPRT 54-55, COST 900-916, ROST 126-130, and EXC 44; preserve remaining cash unless broader follow-through improves.

Held all positions and kept $6,748 cash. April 16 was a broad risk-off session—major technology and semiconductor names fell sharply—and none of the available candidates supplied a convincing fresh breakout, so adding exposure would be premature. The portfolio’s leaders pulled back but did not invalidate their structures: CRWD closed 379.84 after its breakout day and remained above the 360-368 risk zone; TRI held 180.25 near its new high; FAST, CPRT, COST, ROST, WMT, and EXC all remained above their established risk levels. Reconsider on decisive closes below CRWD 360-368, TRI 167-170, FAST 74-76, CPRT 54-55, COST 900-916, ROST 126-130, WMT 85-88, or EXC 44. Deploy cash only after renewed broad follow-through or a strong stock-specific breakout.

Held all positions and retained $6,748 cash. April 17 improved at the margin but did not establish broad follow-through: COST rebounded 2.8% to 994.50 near its session high, EXC advanced to 47.26, and FAST, TRI, WMT, CPRT, and ROST remained constructive, while major growth benchmarks such as AMZN, GOOG, MSFT, NVDA, and AVGO stayed weak. CRWD eased to 375.62 on sharply lighter volume; its breakout has lost momentum but remains above the 360-368 risk zone, so selling now is premature. No unowned candidate offered a superior clean breakout, and the portfolio is already about 86% invested. Reconsider on decisive closes below CRWD 360-368, TRI 167-170, FAST 74-76, CPRT 54-55, COST 900-916, ROST 126-130, WMT 85-88, or EXC 44; deploy cash after sustained breadth or a strong stock-specific breakout.

Exited CRWD after its April 15 breakout failed. It fell 3.4% on April 21 to 362.69, traded as low as 355.66, and closed inside the previously defined 360-368 exit zone; the position is also about 6% below its 386.11 cost. Broad conditions remain hostile: AMZN, MSFT, NVDA, META, AVGO, and many other growth names extended their declines, so preserving the proceeds is preferable to immediate replacement. NFLX showed notable relative strength and heavy volume but faded from 1019 to 987.91 beneath substantial 1000-1060 resistance, so it is not yet a clean breakout. Held EXC, CPRT, COST, ROST, WMT, FAST, and TRI because they remain above established risk levels. Reconsider CRWD only after a convincing reclaim of roughly 380-393; consider NFLX on a decisive high-volume close above 1028-1065. Existing risk levels remain EXC 44, CPRT 54-55, COST 900-916, ROST 126-130, WMT 85-88, FAST 74-76, and TRI 167-170.

Bought a $5,000 NFLX position while retaining roughly $6,047 cash. NFLX delivered the universe's clearest stock-specific strength on April 22: it rose 5.3% to 1040.34, closed above the prior 1027-1028 February pivot, held above 1000 throughout the session, and traded 9.37 million shares, nearly triple its quieter pre-breakout volume. The 1064.97 intraday high tested the February peak near 1064.50, so this is an initial position rather than a full commitment; add only after a decisive close above 1065 or a constructive retest. Exit or reduce if it decisively loses roughly 987-1000, which would negate the breakout. Held EXC, CPRT, COST, ROST, WMT, FAST, and TRI because all remain above their established risk levels. Broad participation improved on April 22 but still needs follow-through, supporting the remaining cash reserve.

Held all eight positions and retained $6,046.88 cash. April 23 extended the broad rebound, and every holding remains above its established risk level. NFLX followed its high-volume breakout with a constructive 0.9% gain to 1049.59, stayed above 1032 intraday, and closed near the upper half of its range; it remains just below 1065 resistance, so neither adding nor exiting is warranted yet. CPRT advanced to 61.05 and WMT held 94.96, while EXC, COST, ROST, FAST, and TRI remain constructive despite modest pauses. Several growth candidates rebounded sharply, but many—including CRWD, PLTR, and major semiconductors—remain near overhead resistance after volatile declines, and much of the April 23 advance came via opening gaps that faded, so preserving a 12.5% cash reserve is preferable to chasing. Add NFLX only after a decisive close above roughly 1065 or a constructive retest; reduce it on a decisive loss of 987-1000. Existing risk levels remain EXC 44, CPRT 54-55, COST 900-916, ROST 126-130, WMT 85-88, FAST 74-76, and TRI 167-170. Deploy cash if the rebound develops sustained breadth or another clean, high-volume breakout.

Added $4,000 to NFLX after the confirmation specified in prior journals. On April 24 it rose 4.5% to 1096.87, decisively cleared the 1064-1065 February resistance area, closed near the 1101 session high, and sustained elevated 6.38 million-share volume. This converts the initial breakout position into a larger holding while preserving about $2,074 cash. Broader confirmation also improved: semiconductors, software, and megacap growth advanced broadly for a third rebound session, although many remain below prior highs, so I did not chase a second name. Held EXC, CPRT, COST, ROST, WMT, FAST, and TRI; all remain above established risk levels. Treat roughly 1040-1065 as first support for the NFLX addition and reduce the added exposure if that breakout zone fails decisively; a loss of 987-1000 would invalidate the overall setup. Existing risk levels remain EXC 44, CPRT 54-55, COST 900-916, ROST 126-130, WMT 85-88, FAST 74-76, and TRI 167-170.

Held all eight positions and the $2,074 cash reserve. NFLX confirmed its breakout with a tight April 25 session: it held 1091, closed at 1101.53 near the high, and remains well above the 1040-1065 support zone. Every other holding remains above its established risk level. Broad growth participation continued, but the strongest alternatives are poorly placed for a new opening buy: PLTR at 112.78 is nearing its February 118-125 resistance after rising about 24% in four sessions; TSLA surged 9.8% to 284.95 into prior March resistance; MSTR reached 368.71 near substantial 380-400 overhead; and CDNS reached 289.63 after two sharp gains but is entering its 290-310 January/February supply area. With cash already only 4.3% of account value, chasing these moves offers inferior risk/reward. Continue to hold NFLX while above 1040-1065 and reduce if that zone fails decisively; 987-1000 remains full invalidation. Existing risk levels remain EXC 44, CPRT 54-55, COST 900-916, ROST 126-130, WMT 85-88, FAST 74-76, and TRI 167-170. Reconsider deployment after a constructive pullback or a decisive breakout through the cited overhead zones.

Held all eight positions and the $2,074 cash reserve. NFLX extended its confirmed breakout on April 28, reaching 1114 and closing at 1110.38; although it briefly tested 1082.62, it remains comfortably above the 1040-1065 breakout/support zone. EXC, COST, ROST, WMT, FAST, and TRI were stable and remain above their established risk levels. CPRT pulled back for a second session to 59.81 after its 61.97 close, but it remains above nearby 58-59 support and well above the 54-55 risk zone, so the move does not warrant an exit. Growth breadth paused rather than broke: CRWD, CDNS, NVDA, and MSTR softened, while PLTR, PANW, APP, and ZS advanced; the stronger names are extended into resistance after rapid rebounds, making a new opening buy unattractive with only 4.3% cash. Continue holding NFLX above 1040-1065 and reduce if that zone fails decisively; 987-1000 remains full invalidation. Other risk levels remain EXC 44, CPRT 54-55, COST 900-916, ROST 126-130, WMT 85-88, FAST 74-76, and TRI 167-170. Reconsider deployment after a constructive pullback or clean breakout from a new base.

Held all eight positions and $2,074.13 cash. At the April 29 close, every holding remained above its established risk level: EXC 46.85, CPRT 60.51, COST 991.70, ROST 140.78, WMT 96.04, FAST 80.28, TRI 184.30, and NFLX 1125.64. NFLX continues to hold decisively above its 1040-1065 breakout/support zone, while CPRT recovered to 60.51 and remains above nearby 58-59 support. I am not deploying the small residual cash because leading alternatives have already rebounded into overhead areas: PLTR is 116.08 near 118-125 resistance, MSTR is 381.45 near 380-400 supply, TSLA is 292.03 in prior resistance, and CDNS at 302.22 is extended into its former 290-310 supply zone. Preserve flexibility rather than chase immediately before the next monthly funding session. Reduce NFLX if 1040-1065 fails decisively, with 987-1000 as full invalidation. Other risk levels remain EXC 44, CPRT 54-55, COST 900-916, ROST 126-130, WMT 85-88, FAST 74-76, and TRI 167-170. Reassess allocation when new cash arrives and after observing whether recent growth breakouts consolidate constructively.

Deployed $42,000 of the new monthly cash across six positions and retained about $10,074 before opening-price effects; held all eight existing positions because each remains above its prior risk level. TTWO closed 233.32 after clearing the 218-221 multi-month ceiling and making a 100-session high. ZS closed 226.17 after breaking above its prior 215-217 highs, with a steady sequence of higher closes. CRWD consolidated tightly at 428.87 after its April 24 breakout above 400-415; it remains below February's 455 high, so position size is controlled. VRTX closed 509.50 after reclaiming 500 and provides non-technology diversification. MNST closed 60.12 near its 100-session high after a long base and a volume-supported move through 59-60. MELI is only a pilot because 2330.85 is near February's 2374.54 high, but the April 30 advance had strong volume and held above the 2200-2240 pivot. New risk levels: reduce TTWO if 218-221 fails and exit on a decisive break below 210-212; ZS if 215-217 fails, with 200-205 full invalidation; CRWD below 412-415, then 395-400; VRTX below 490-500, then 480; MNST below 58-59, then 56.5-57; MELI below 2200-2240, with 2100-2130 full invalidation. Existing levels remain EXC 44, CPRT 54-55, COST 900-916, ROST 126-130, WMT 85-88, FAST 74-76, TRI 167-170, and NFLX 1040-1065 with 987-1000 full invalidation. Add only after constructive holds or clean breakouts; do not chase sharp opening gaps.

journal.text: Held all 14 positions and the $10,080.86 cash reserve one session after the major monthly deployment. The new breakouts remain constructive: TTWO closed 235.17 above its 218-221 pivot, ZS 227.06 above 215-217, and CRWD 431.88 above 412-415. MNST's 59.52 close remains above 58-59 support, while MELI at 2294.52 remains above its 2200-2240 pivot. VRTX reversed from 509.50 to 498.86, but its 498.21 intraday low and close are still within the planned 490-500 support area rather than a decisive breakdown; do not sell after one test. Existing holdings also remain above their risk levels, and NFLX held its breakout at 1133.47. Because the portfolio is already about 90% invested and yesterday added six names, preserve cash rather than chase another strong rebound. Reconsider VRTX on a decisive close below 490, MNST below 58-59, MELI below 2200-2240, TTWO below 218-221, ZS below 215-217, or CRWD below 412-415; otherwise allow the new positions time to consolidate.

Held all 14 positions and $10,080.86 cash. TTWO was the only material warning: it gapped down to 214.45 on unusually heavy 8.97M volume, traded as low as 211, but recovered to close at 219.50 inside the established 218-221 pivot. Because it did not decisively close below support, avoid selling the first violent retest; reduce on a close below 218 and exit on a decisive break below 210-212. The other recent additions remain constructive: ZS 230.47 and CRWD 440.58 advanced above their breakouts, VRTX stabilized at 501.15, MNST held 60.05, and MELI at 2280.69 remains above 2200-2240 support. Existing positions also remain above their risk levels, with NFLX at 1156.49, COST at 1008.30, and WMT at 98.75 showing particular strength. Preserve the roughly 10% cash reserve rather than chase strength. Reconsider VRTX below 490, MNST below 58, MELI below 2200, ZS below 215-217, or CRWD below 412-415.

Held all 14 positions and $10,080.86 cash. The May 5 tape confirmed rather than invalidated the portfolio: TTWO rebounded from its prior high-volume support test, closing 225.32 after holding 217.74 intraday, back above the 218-221 pivot. ZS advanced to 232.98, CRWD to 443.47, MNST to 60.91, COST to 1014.89, and WMT to 99.33; these trends do not warrant chasing with the remaining reserve. MELI weakened for a third session to 2246.54, with a 2242.50 low, but remains at the planned 2200-2240 support zone rather than below it. VRTX remains stable near 500, and NFLX recovered substantially from an opening gap down to close 1134.06. Keep the roughly 10% cash buffer after the recent six-name deployment. Reconsider MELI on a decisive close below 2200, TTWO below 218 and especially 210-212, VRTX below 490, MNST below 58, ZS below 215-217, or CRWD below 412-415; otherwise continue holding the constructive mix.

Exited the full VRTX position and redeployed $6,000 into MSFT, with the sell ordered first and the remaining roughly $10,000 cash reserve preserved. VRTX invalidated the planned setup decisively on May 6: it gapped from 500.19 to 465.56, traded down to 428.55, and closed 450.03 on 8.0M shares, far below both the 490-500 first-risk zone and 480 full-invalidation level. This is not an ordinary support test, so capital should be removed despite the loss. MSFT offers a stronger replacement setup: its May 1 earnings gap lifted it from 395.26 to a 425.40 close on 58.9M shares, and the next three sessions held the gap while closing 435.28, 436.17, and 433.31. The position is sized near 6% rather than chased aggressively. Reduce MSFT if it decisively loses the 424-425 gap-day low/close area; a break toward 415 and especially back below 400 would invalidate the setup. Continue holding all other positions: FAST's sharp decline to 78.50 remains above its 74-76 risk zone, MELI at 2229 remains above 2200, and TTWO, ZS, and CRWD remain constructive.

Held all 14 positions and $10,259.64 cash. The portfolio remains constructive enough that neither turnover nor use of the roughly 10% reserve is justified. CRWD was the principal warning: it gapped down, fell to 417.06, and closed 422.52 on elevated 6.67M volume, but it still held the previously defined 412-415 breakout/risk area; reduce or exit on a decisive close below that zone rather than react above support. FAST stabilized at 78.50 after Tuesday's decline and remains above its 74-76 invalidation area. TTWO pulled back to 226.34 but stayed above the 218-221 pivot, while MELI rebounded from 2217.46 to 2262.09 on stronger volume, confirming its 2200 support for now. MSFT held its earnings gap at 433.35, and ZS, NFLX, TRI, ROST, WMT, COST, CPRT, EXC, and MNST retain intact trends or bases. Preserve cash for a clearer setup. Reconsider MSFT below 424-425, MELI below 2200, TTWO below 218 and especially 210-212, ZS below 215-217, MNST below 58, FAST below 74-76, or CRWD below 412-415.

Opened a $3,000 starter position in AXON while retaining roughly $7,273 cash and all existing holdings. AXON produced the cleanest fresh leadership signal in the reviewed universe: on May 8 it gapped from the prior 601.82 close to 646.38, reached 698.27, and closed 686.83 near the session high on 1.69M shares, more than double recent volume and above its prior 638.35 high. The modest roughly 3% sizing recognizes overnight gap and post-earnings volatility rather than chasing at full size. Reconsider AXON on a close below the 644-646 gap-day low/open area, and exit on a decisive loss of the 620-628 prior base. Existing positions remain valid: MELI's high-volume gap to 2410 strengthens its breakout, CRWD recovered to 428.63 above 412-415 support, MSFT held its earnings gap, and TTWO, ZS, FAST, and MNST remain above stated risk levels. EXC's 45.10 close and the pullbacks in WMT/COST warrant monitoring but not sales yet.

Exited CRWD and redeployed $6,000 into CEG, with the sell ordered first and a meaningful cash reserve retained. CRWD triggered the previously defined risk rule: after the May 7 high-volume break, its May 9 rebound failed, it traded down to 404.63 and closed at 410.57 below the 412-415 support zone on 4.69M shares. Two sharp declines within three sessions make this a failed breakout rather than a routine pause. CEG offers stronger current leadership: it advanced from 223.44 on April 30 to 273.82 on May 6 with expanding 7.20M volume, then consolidated constructively for three sessions at 268.12, 270.59, and 271.37 without losing the May 6 gap-day low near 256. Position size is moderate because CEG is extended after a fast advance. Reconsider CEG on a close below 256-260; a decisive loss of 247-250 would invalidate the breakout. Hold the remaining positions; AXON and MELI are sustaining their earnings gaps, MSFT remains above 424-425, and TTWO, ZS, FAST, and MNST remain above their stated risk levels.

Exited EXC and initiated a $5,000 NVDA position, with the sale ordered first and roughly an 11% cash reserve expected to remain. EXC invalidated its prior defensive uptrend: after closing near 47 in late April, it fell through 45 and on May 12 closed at 43.61 near the 43.34 low on 9.91M shares, the heaviest volume of the past month. NVDA offers materially stronger relative momentum: it cleared the 117-119 resistance area and closed at the session high of 123 on 225M shares, confirming a breakout from its late-April/early-May consolidation. Dollar sizing limits overnight gap exposure. Reconsider NVDA on a close back below 115-117, with a decisive loss of 110-112 invalidating the setup. Hold other positions: CEG remains above 256-260, AXON above its 644-646 gap area, MSFT above 424-425, and TTWO recovered from a 219.41 intraday test to close 226.25. Monitor NFLX after its higher-volume decline; a decisive loss of roughly 1095-1100 would warrant action.

Initiated a $5,000 APP position from cash, leaving roughly a 6% reserve while retaining all existing holdings. APP delivered the clearest fresh breakout among reviewed leaders: after its May 8 earnings gap, it absorbed a pullback to 328.54, recovered to 347.90, then surged 6.4% on May 13 to close 370.10 near the 380.70 high on 9.73M shares. That close decisively cleared both the May 8 high of 357.64 and the March peak near 352, while the higher-volume advance supports confirmation rather than a low-volume chase. Dollar sizing limits unknown opening-gap exposure. Reconsider APP on a close back below roughly 343-348; a decisive loss of 328-335 would invalidate the breakout. Existing positions remain valid: NVDA confirmed its breakout with a high-volume rise to 129.93, AXON and CEG reached new highs, ZS advanced to 245, and NFLX rebounded above its 1095-1100 risk area. Monitor WMT near 94-95 and FAST near 78, but neither has decisively broken support.

Held all positions and retained the $5,809 cash reserve. The portfolio’s leaders remain technically intact: APP followed its May 13 breakout with a further rise to 376.54, NVDA extended to 135.34 on 281M shares, AXON held near its new high, MELI closed at a fresh 2564 high, and MSFT advanced to 452.94. CEG’s modest pullback stayed well above the 256-260 risk area, while NFLX recovered to 1150.99 and remains above 1095-1100. Weaker holdings still have not invalidated: FAST continues to hold 78 support, WMT rebounded to 96.83 after testing 95.23, TTWO improved to 229.50, and COST remains above the recent 987.60 low. I avoided chasing sharp two-day advances in PLTR, TSLA, ARM, and other semiconductor names after the portfolio already added NVDA and APP this week. Reconsider FAST on a decisive close below 78, WMT below 94-95, COST below roughly 987, TTWO below 219-220, APP below 343-348, and CEG below 256-260.

Held all positions and the $5,817.53 cash reserve. The May 15 evidence remains constructive: NFLX broke to a new high at 1177.98, while CPRT, ROST, TRI, and MNST also closed at or near fresh highs. WMT’s earnings-related gap down reversed sharply from 91.89 to 96.35 on 44.0M shares, so the prior 94-95 close-based risk level was not breached. APP’s decline to 366.61 was an orderly first pullback after its breakout and remained above 361 intraday and the 343-348 support zone. NVDA consolidated near 135 after its high-volume advance, and CEG’s three-day pullback stayed above 283 and well above its 256-260 invalidation area. I did not deploy the small reserve because many unowned leaders, including semiconductors and PLTR, are extended after rapid advances, while the portfolio already has broad exposure and no holding has invalidated. Reconsider APP below 343-348, NVDA below 115-117, CEG below 256-260, NFLX below 1095-1100, TTWO below 219-220, FAST below 78, COST below 983-987, and WMT on a decisive close below roughly 92-94.

Held all positions and the $5,817.53 cash reserve. Friday’s evidence remained broadly constructive: NFLX, CPRT, ROST, TRI, and MNST closed at or near fresh highs; ZS advanced 2.3% to 251.50; WMT followed its earnings reversal with a 2.0% gain to 98.24; and COST and FAST strengthened away from their recent support tests.
